name: CASA C-212 Aviocar
summary: Spanish high-wing twin turboprop with a rear loading ramp, a fixed landing gear and a boxy fuselage, flown by cargo operators, skydivers and government agencies.

wings: Engines mounted at the wing leading edge
engines: Two Garrett TPE331 turboprops in nacelles that stretch ahead of and behind the wing
fuselage: Boxy, rectangular-section fuselage with a blunt, flat-fronted nose
Fixed main landing gear in blister sponsons on the lower fuselage
Rear fuselage sweeps up to a loading ramp and tail
tail: Tailplane set on the upswept rear fuselage

tellTales: Boxy fuselage sweeping up to a rear ramp, with a single tall fin
High unbraced wing with engines on the leading edge
Fixed main gear in blisters on the lower fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Dornier 228 has a long, pointed nose and no rear ramp; the C-212 has a blunt flat-faced nose and an upswept rear ramp.
The Skyvan has twin fins and wing struts; the C-212 has one fin and no struts.
The Shorts has wing struts and engines on top of the wing; the C-212 has an unbraced wing with engines at the leading edge.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
